question: Do changes in old A retention remain under identical physical support actions and tastes?
models: The uniform start, all three latest common continuation arms and both reciprocal uniform/native body/write-rule swaps. Use all six paired births of each cohort.
protocol: In each birth use the frozen uniform parent to generate an ordinary eight-contact action stream on the sealed odor tape. Replay exactly these physical motor sides, current sensory menus, private tastes and write proposal draws for each tested graph. Allow the first A contact to write in every branch. From that common A state, compare later writes, identical later contacts with their writes disabled, and equal elapsed neutral waits. At each cut independently probe actual A choices after the standard four-tick wait, with the same probe draw. Report trial scores, write minus sham, and stage minus start at matched branches. Paired contrasts also compare changes in the decrement relative to the same graph immediately after learning A.
scope: Forced-side replay is a mechanism intervention. Normal physical motor choices remain in the separate frozen score card. Distinguish poor acquisition at cut 1 from excess change after further observations. The write rule and body are inherited together in both original models.
